newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - STET jumps in New York trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - STET jumps in New York trade.

text.p: Shares in Italian telecom holding STET jumped in New York on Monday on news of a merger with Telecom Italia, traders said.
STET's American Depositary Receipt rose 2-1/4 to 37-5/8 after Italy said it would merge state-controlled STET and Telecom Italia by May 1997. STET has a majority holding in Telecom Italia.
STET's privatization was moved back to autumn 1997 from early next year.

Among other telecom stocks, Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd rose 1-1/8 to 17-5/8 after a British newspaper said Cable and Wireless Plc would cut its 58.6 percent stake to less than 50 percent, with the buyer an unnamed Chinese party.
Cable and Wireless would get better access to the Chinese market. Hong Kong Telecom called the report groundless and Cable and Wireless' ADR was unchanged at 23-3/4.
Latin American stocks were largely quiet because the New York bond market was closed for the Veterans Day holiday and because many companies are reporting quarterly earnings.
"I think it's a day characterized by not a whole lot of news," said Javier Leon, head of sales at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Mexican ADRs firmed slightly on a stronger peso and state elections carried out on Sunday without violence.
Telefonos de Mexico SA rose 1/4 to 31-1/2. Coca-Cola FEMSA was up 1/2 to 25-1/2, also helped by CS First Boston's upgrade of the stock to a buy from hold.
Argentina's Banco de Galicia y Buenos Aires rose 3/8 to 19-1/4 after reporting improved first-quarter earnings.
Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy rose 1-1/4 to 51-1/8 amid hopes for strong interim earnings.
There were 435 advancing and 216 declining stocks in an index of 807 shares at midday. Volume was 25.7 million shares.
